title: Operations Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll meet the four methods of production and learn what productivity really measures.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies operations foundations — job, batch, flow, mass production and productivity.
final_note: You can identify methods of production, define productivity and explain how it's measured.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pick a method based on volume and customisation.

Job: one-off, high-skill. Batch: groups (bread loaves). Flow: continuous (cars). Mass: huge volumes (drinks cans).

Productivity = output ÷ input. Usually output per worker per hour.

If 4 workers make 200 units in an 8-hour day, productivity = 200 ÷ (4 × 8) = 6.25 units/worker/hour.

Higher productivity = lower cost per unit = bigger margins or lower prices.

It's boosted by training, motivation, better tech, lean processes, and good management.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
options: Fixed costs are paid every month and variable costs are paid weekly.
Fixed costs do not change with output level (e.g. rent, salaries); variable costs change in proportion to output (e.g. raw materials, hourly wages).
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Fixed costs are the cheapest costs and variable costs are the most expensive.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
